title: Consolidate request pipeline and TTL-driven KV grooming
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Over the last 18 months we incrementally added specialized request lanes, ad-hoc prefetch hooks, and multiple eviction heuristics into the KV subsystem. This resulted in fragile interactions: leases are renewed in three different places, prefetch races sometimes inflate KV working set, and TTL/age accounting is duplicated across components.

Goal: Simplify the request pipeline into a single canonical path for continuous-batching requests, and introduce a TTL-driven KV grooming adapter that centralizes eviction decisions and lease lifecycle. The refactor should reduce code duplication, eliminate redundant lease renewals, and reduce tail latency variance caused by spurious prefetch/backpressure interactions.

Scope:
- Combine prefetch and slot-allocation logic into a single RequestCoordinator module.
- Replace per-lane eviction callbacks with a TTL-driven KVGroomer that runs across shards.
- Unify lease acquisition/renewal into a LeaseManager with clear ownership rules.
- Migrate existing tests and add end-to-end scenarios for race conditions (prefetch vs eviction) and lease expiry.
- Ensure compatibility with Dedicated mode (reserved pools) and Private deployments (VPC networking).
acceptance_criteria: Single RequestCoordinator handles continuous-batching flow and exposes a small surface for prefetch hints
KVGroomer makes eviction decisions based on shard-level TTL, last-access-time, and active-lease counts
No duplicate lease-renewal paths in production code (audit and static checks pass)
End-to-end load test shows <=5% increase in median latency and >=10% reduction in 99.9th percentile KV miss spike rate under synthetic prefetch-heavy workloads
Rolling migration plan exists so nodes can move to new protocol without downtime
implementation_notes: Phased approach: 1) introduce RequestCoordinator as opt-in behind feature-flag, keep existing lanes active; 2) implement LeaseManager and run audits to detect dual renewal; 3) wire in KVGroomer and run in read-only mode to collect metrics for two weeks; 4) flip KVGroomer to active eviction after metrics validate. Use compile-time feature toggles for Dedicated vs Hosted differences. Keep new modules small, with well-defined interfaces to facilitate code review. Avoid changing kernel selection or batching heuristics in this ticket — only orchestration and lease/eviction surfaces.
migration_plan:
- Stage 0: deploy RequestCoordinator behind feature flag to 10% of nodes and mirror traffic.
- Stage 1: route a small fraction (5%) of continuous-batching requests through RequestCoordinator with dual-write lease ops for audit.
- Stage 2: enable KVGroomer in read-only mode to collect eviction candidates and compare to current evictions.
- Stage 3: roll out LeaseManager and turn off duplicate renewal paths.
- Stage 4: enable active KVGroomer with conservative thresholds and observe for 48 hours per cohort.
- Rollback: revert feature flag and LeaseManager toggle; KVGroomer can be switched to read-only mode instantly.
test_plan: Unit tests for RequestCoordinator state transitions and prefetch hint semantics
Integration tests simulating lease contention across shards
Chaos tests that randomly drop lease-renew RPCs to verify graceful recovery
Cluster-scale soak test with mixed batch sizes and synthetic prefetch pattern to validate 99.9th latency behavior
Compatibility smoke tests for Dedicated and Private modes (auth, KMS access)
metrics: Lease renewal rate and duplicate-renewal violations (should be zero)
99.9th token generation latency under prefetch-heavy workloads
Eviction churn (evictions per minute) and working-set size
RequestCoordinator queue depth and batching efficiency
